review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for uses of the map_comp/id lemmas. The finding is about inconsistent simp coverage of the functoriality lemmas. I did not run Lean, so I did not check how the simp set behaves once the attribute is added. The other simp lemmas (topObj_forget, toPresheafedSpace_obj/map, the simps-generated lemmas) looked reasonable. I did not find any rewrite cycles or competing rules.

findings.excerpt:
theorem Spec.sheafedSpaceMap_comp {R S T : CommRingCat.{u}} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : S ⟶ T) :
    Spec.sheafedSpaceMap (f ≫ g) = Spec.sheafedSpaceMap g ≫ Spec.sheafedSpaceMap f
findings.problem: The functoriality lemmas for the three levels of Spec are inconsistently tagged. `Spec.topMap_id`, `Spec.topMap_comp` and `Spec.sheafedSpaceMap_id` are all `@[simp]`, but `Spec.sheafedSpaceMap_comp` is not. The same gap exists for `Spec.locallyRingedSpaceMap_id` (simp) versus `Spec.locallyRingedSpaceMap_comp` (not simp). As a result, `Spec.toSheafedSpace` has to pass the lemma by hand with `simp [Spec.sheafedSpaceMap_comp]`, and `Spec.toLocallyRingedSpace` uses `rw`. The right-hand side is a composite of smaller terms, so the rule terminates and gives the same normal form as `topMap_comp`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `Spec.sheafedSpaceMap_comp`, and probably also to `Spec.locallyRingedSpaceMap_comp`, to match the `_id` and `topMap_comp` lemmas. Then `map_comp f g := by simp` can replace `simp [Spec.sheafedSpaceMap_comp]`. If the attribute is deliberately withheld, for example because simp would unfold `(f ≫ g)` too eagerly in downstream scheme files, add a comment saying so.
findings.benefit: Users who simp goals about `Spec.sheafedSpaceMap (f ≫ g)` or `Spec.locallyRingedSpaceMap (f ≫ g)` get the same normal form as at the topological level, without naming the lemma each time. The simp interface for identity and composition also becomes uniform across the three levels.
